column1: QB2 Model Support Requirements - qwen3.8-27b (agentic coding)   ·   Rev 0.11

Actual requirements for qwen3.8-27b on TT-QuietBox 2, scoped to the agentic coding use-case. Targets are mildly aggressive: set ~10% better than a measured single-accelerator reference and held within QB2's decode roofline. Every eval number is from the HF model card; every perf anchor is from the cited benchmark or an explicitly labeled roofline derivation. Numbers labeled 'target' are requirements, not measurements.

column2: 27B dense (28B incl. vision encoder); causal LM + native vision encoder [1]

Hybrid: 64 layers = 16 x (3x Gated DeltaNet + 1x Gated Attention). Only the 16 full-attention layers carry a context-growing KV cache (4 KV heads, head dim 256); the 48 DeltaNet layers use fixed-size state. [1]
VLM; text + image + video in, text out (coding use-case is text-dominant) [1]
262,144 tokens native; extensible to ~1,000,000 via YaRN [1]

column1: Agent-harness coding loop: read repository context, call tools, apply edits over multiple steps. Workload basis: TraceLab (arXiv:2606.30560) Table 8 / sec 5.2 - per-step median output 252 tokens for Claude (184 for Codex), p90 < 1.7k; ~8 tool-steps per request; each step replays a large cached prefix (Claude P50 ~126K) and appends < 1K new tokens. Implication: prefix caching is mandatory (see Section 3 notes), and steady-state latency is decode-bound once the prefix is cached. [2]

column2: Batch 1 = agentic coding without subagents (single request). Batch 8-16 = agentic coding with subagents (agent fans out to parallel subagent calls) at short/mid context (<=32K); taper to <=8 for long (>=128K) sessions. [2][4]

column1: Pass if the QB2-served FP8 checkpoint scores within tolerance of the HF model-card reference. Tolerance: -5% relative to the reference (e.g. 61.7 -> pass at >= 58.6). column1: * The card reports SWE-bench Pro (61.7); the tt-inference-server CI task is SWE-bench Verified. Align the variant before gating: either run Pro to match the 61.7 reference, or obtain the card's Verified score. Terminal-Bench 2.1, LiveCodeBench v6, and GPQA-Diamond map directly to CI tasks. [1]
Batch 1 - agentic coding without subagents (single request)
Warm-prefill TTFT targets - batch 1, agentic coding without subagents (APC hit: <= 1K appended over cached prefix)

Warm-prefill TTFT = TTFT when the prefix is already cached (APC) and only the appended tokens (<1K, per TraceLab) are prefilled. It tracks the ~1K-ISL cold row, roughly flat vs cached-prefix size, with a modest rise at long ISL from attention over the longer cached KV. Grounded in the reference caching note: adding ~1K new tokens to a long cached context yields TTFT near the 1K result, not the full-ISL result. Measure via the vLLM prefix_repetition benchmark at concurrency 1 (Section 3 cache-efficiency block). [4][7]
Batch 8 - agentic coding with subagents (agent + parallel subagents)

Batch-8 requirement (agentic coding with subagents): sustain 8 concurrent requests (agent + parallel subagents) with per-user decode >= 20 t/s (the reference's agentic-coding usability floor) at coding-typical context. Per-user targets 34/28/22 t/s (at 4K/32K/128K) sit under the QB2 roofline below and above the floor; aggregate = per-user x 8. Cold TTFT under load also carries queue wait (chunked prefill, Section 4, bounds its p99); APC keeps warm-step TTFT at the 128-ISL value. [4]
Batch 16 - agentic coding with subagents, max concurrency (short/mid context)

Batch-16 requirement: viable for short/mid context - per-user decode 32/24 t/s at 4K/32K (aggregate 512/384), above the 20 t/s floor. At 128K, per-user decode approaches the ~22 t/s roofline and realistically falls below the floor, and KV for 16 x 128K (~64 GB) + weights (27 GB) = ~91 GB leaves little headroom; cap concurrency at <=8 for long (>=128K) sessions. [3][4]
Cache-efficiency benchmark (vLLM prefix_repetition) - warm vs cold prefill

column2: REQUIRED. >90% of coding steps append <1K over a large cached prefix; without APC, long-context cold TTFT (up to ~60s @256K) makes agentic loops unusable. [2][4]
REQUIRED. Interleave long prefills with decode so a cache-miss prefill does not stall other users; heavily impacts user-observed TTFT p99, especially at batch 8. [4]
262,144 (native). Extend toward 1M via YaRN only when the workload needs it (static YaRN can dent short-context quality). [1]
Size to the chunked-prefill chunk so one long prefill does not monopolize a step; tune against the TTFT targets above. [4]

REQUIRED. The card ships MTP weights; enable to lift per-user decode above the memory-bandwidth roofline (spec decode verifies multiple tokens per weight-read). Section 3 decode targets are set WITHOUT spec-decode credit (from the no-MTP reference + roofline), so MTP is headroom toward and above them; verify token acceptance rate and realized speedup on QB2. [1][4]

column1: Roof-line feasibility check (targets vs QB2 limits)

Decode is bandwidth-bound. Per step the device reads the 27 GB FP8 weights once (amortized across the batch) plus the KV cache for all active sequences; per-user ceiling = batch / (bytes-per-step / 2,048 GB/s) / batch. KV lives only in the 16 full-attention layers = 2 x 4 KV heads x 256 head dim x 16 = 32 KB/token (FP8), ~4 GB per 128K sequence. [1][3]

Rows are supported operating points. Batch 16 is capped at short/mid context (<= 32K); at 128K, per-user decode cannot clear the 20 t/s floor, so >= 128K is served at <= batch 8 (see Section 3 batch-16 note).

Memory fit: batch 8 @128K = 27 GB weights + 8 x 4 GB KV = ~59 GB, inside 128 GB GDDR6 (excludes small fixed DeltaNet state and activations); this is why batch 8 at long context is viable on QB2. Cold TTFT tracks the reference's ~9,850 t/s peak prefill; QB2 (2,654 TFLOPS BlockFP8) is the same class, and APC removes cold prefill from the steady-state path. Ceilings above are non-spec-decode; required MTP (Section 4) verifies multiple tokens per weight-read and can push per-user decode above them. [1][3][4]
